issue.title: test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2 fails on master: asserts unwrapped 'Aliases follow in parentheses.' against wrapped Tier 2 output

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic and static: the assertion compares a fixed literal against text rendered from a fixed in-repo template, with no timing, ordering, concurrency, or I/O involved. Reproduced twice on the same clean tree at HEAD af951d1f9 — once inside the full parallel 'just test' run and once in isolation with '-p no:randomly' (2.34s, same AssertionError, same wrapped text). git log -S confirms the assertion and the rendered string were introduced together by 445afde7c, so it has been failing since that commit rather than intermittently.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-pm — the other live failure from the same unrelated Tier 2 memory-rendering work (commits 538dec9fc / 445afde7c). sase-pm is the symvision gate on src/sase/amd/_agents_doc.py; this bead is the pytest gate on the rendered output. A fix that reflows or restructures the Tier 2 template could move this assertion again, so whoever works either one should check the other.

RELATED: sase-p5 — discovered by that epic's land agent while running 'just test' on the epic's combined tree. Not caused by sase-p5: git log -S shows the assertion and the rendered string were introduced together by the non-bead commit 445afde7c, and sase-p5's commits touch only src/sase/workflows/commit/ and src/sase/llm_provider/commit_finalizer*.

evidence.note: Independently reproduced on workspace sase_19 at HEAD 134839e82 while verifying the launch-control-setting-labels tale. just test-scoped escalated to the full suite (core-identity-changed) and failed only this node: tests/main/test_init_memory_glossary.py::test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2. AssertionError is the same wrap: expected unwrapped 'Aliases follow in parentheses.' but the rendered Tier 2 block has 'Aliases follow\nin parentheses.'. Working tree only touches Launch Control label strings and their goldens; I did not edit src/sase/amd/ or tests/main/test_init_memory_glossary.py. 33086 other tests passed. This is the same pre-existing master failure already tracked here.

Independent reproduction on 2026-08-18 during sase agent restart implementation. Full suite failed tests/main/test_init_memory_glossary.py::test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2 with AssertionError: assert 'Aliases follow in parentheses.' in the wrapped Tier 2 glossary block ('Aliases follow\nin parentheses.'). This change set does not touch memory glossary rendering. Deterministic, not a flake.

payload.entry: Verified on master HEAD 5c748697f: the original unwrapped assertion from 445afde7c is already gone. cbed33584 made the check wrap-tolerant via 'Aliases follow in parentheses.' in ' '.join(tier2.split()), matching the rendered Tier 2 wrap ('Aliases follow\nin parentheses.' in AGENTS.md). Isolated rerun of tests/main/test_init_memory_glossary.py::test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2 passed (0.28s call); the full glossary file is 10 passed. No remaining product or test change required.

fields.description:
`tests/main/test_init_memory_glossary.py::test_memory_plan_renders_glossary_terms_block_in_tier2`
fails deterministically on master (HEAD af951d1f9). Discovered while landing epic
sase-p5 (`just test` on the epic's combined tree: 1 failed, 33079 passed, 12 skipped).

Failure:

    assert "Aliases follow in parentheses." in tier2
    AssertionError: ... 'definition plus every term the definition depends on. Aliases follow\nin parentheses.\n\n- Agent Clan (clan)\n- Workspace\n'

Root cause: the rendered Tier 2 glossary block is line-wrapped, so the sentence
"Aliases follow in parentheses." is split across a newline between "follow" and
"in". The test asserts the unwrapped literal substring, which no longer occurs in
the rendered output. Every other assertion in the test (the `### 2.1 Long-Term
Memory Files` / `### 2.2 Glossary Terms` headings, their ordering, the
`sase glossary read` snippet) passes; only this one substring assertion fails.

Introduced by 445afde7c ("feat: Split Tier 2 into 'Long-Term Memory Files' and
'Glossary Terms' H3 sections"), the only commit touching both the assertion and
the rendered source string; the markdown reflow that wraps the sentence arrived
with the same Tier 2 rendering work (see also 28613d6fb, "chore: Format with
prettier"). Neither commit carries a SASE_BEAD footer, so no bead owns this work.

Scope: decide whether the fix is the test (assert against wrap-insensitive text,
e.g. normalize whitespace before the containment check, matching how the sibling
assertions are written) or the renderer (emit the sentence unwrapped). Prefer
making the assertion wrap-insensitive unless the wrap is itself unintended, since
the surrounding template is prettier-formatted and will re-wrap on any width change.
